sections.heading: Shipping AI-generated code without losing assurance?
sections.body: AI-assisted changes still need to meet your functional, security and release standards. A faster coding cycle can outpace review capacity, while dependencies and generated changes add questions about what is safe to release.

sections.heading: Make release decisions on evidence
sections.body: The intended outcome is a traceable release decision for AI-written change, with quality and security gates across CI/CD. Agree what must pass, what needs human review and who can accept an exception. Measure against your own baseline using regression coverage, unresolved findings and gate results, rather than coding speed alone.

items.title: Can this fit our current CI/CD toolchain?
items.description: Start by reviewing your repositories, pipeline stages and testing tools. The engagement defines integration points for testoriumz and VectorX, alongside checks that remain in your existing toolchain.

items.title: Does AI-generated code need a different release standard?
items.description: Your business and risk owners define the release standard. We help identify where AI-assisted changes need additional review, regression coverage or supply-chain analysis, without removing human accountability.

items.title: What evidence would we receive?
items.description: The agreed scope can include test results, scan findings, remediation status and release-gate decisions. The evidence pack records accepted exceptions and the owner of each unresolved item.

items.title: Where should we start?
items.description: Bring one representative repository, its pipeline and a critical user journey. A scoped assessment can establish the current assurance baseline and prioritise the first gates to implement.
